_comment: Hand-authored. Bank 5 special-screen object: $9F22-$A0F6, the two shop tables, the progress recorder $A2B9-$A2E6 and the move-history test. The generators subtract these.

regions.name: Screen object: first call or a later one
regions.description: SPECIAL-SCREEN OBJECT (bank 5 slot `$8012`, called by bank 6 `$9A12` for object type `$35`; X = its slot): the type byte's bit 7 is set once `$CFA0` has run, so the first call (bit clear) initialises and every later call (bit set) goes to the per-frame code at `$A0AE`. RUN: slot 5 set to type `$35`, `$51` = the screen type, `$E4` = a real map record, bank 5 live, `$9F22` called with X = 5 on the labyrinth savestate.

regions.name: Screen object: initialise by screen type
regions.description: `JSR $C0AE` (`$CFA0`: set bit 7 of the type, load the per-type collision flags, hit points, attack and drawing flags into `$0578 / $0590 / $05A8 / $0620`), then `JSR $9F10` with A = the screen type `$51`: the nine-entry inline jump table at `$9F32` picks the set-up routine.

regions.name: Init, type 8 (the sealed gate)
regions.description: `JSR $9F88` (the gate banner), then slots X and X+1 both become type `$B5` (`$35` plus bit 7, already initialised); in slot X `$0638`, `$0788`, `$0620` := 0 and `$0578` := `$6A`, `$0650` := 1; in slot X+1 (`$0669`, `$0681`, `$0621`) the same fields := 0, 0, 1 and its countdown `$07A1` := 60. Then `JMP $A0F7`, the gate drivers (the two halves; see the seal notes). RUN: slots 5 and 6 = `$B5`, slot 6 `$07A0` = `$3C`, `$0620` = 1. RUN: slot 5 set to type `$35`, `$51` = the screen type, `$E4` = a real map record, bank 5 live, `$9F22` called with X = 5 on the labyrinth savestate.

regions.name: Init, type 5 (the gate just cleared): the reward box
regions.description: `JSR $9F88` (the banner), then slot 5 becomes type `$31` (the pick-up box) at x `$80`, y `$70`; `$55` (the corridor's reward item, `$EF40`) is what it holds. RUN: slot 5 = `$31` at (`$80`, `$70`). RUN: slot 5 set to type `$35`, `$51` = the screen type, `$E4` = a real map record, bank 5 live, `$9F22` called with X = 5 on the labyrinth savestate.

regions.name: Gate banner: start
regions.description: Used by types 4, 5 and 8. `$0788,X` := 0 and `$0620,X` := 6: the state of the banner routine in bank 2.

regions.name: Gate banner: run it
regions.description: `JSR $C045` (wait for the tile decompressor), then a far call (inline `02 08 80`) to bank 2 `$8009` (-> `$82C0`): a state machine on `$0788,X` (not read here; it reads strings via `$8291[$51]` and uses the font expander). It is called again and again from `$9F9B` until `$0788,X` = `$83`.

regions.name: Gate banner: finished?
regions.description: `$0788,X` = `$83` ends it; else back to `$9F92`. RUN: all three gate types returned after 18 frames.

regions.name: Gate banner: remove the object
regions.description: `JSR $C048` (`$CCBF`) removes the banner object (type 4: the whole screen object; types 5 and 8 set the slot up again afterwards).

regions.name: Gate banner: the corridor number
regions.description: `$19:$18` := `$2091`, A := byte 2 of the room record AND `$7F` (the corridor, `$E4` points at the record), `JMP $C051` (`$E1CD`): three digits at PPU `$2091`. This is also the whole of **type 4** (the cleared gate on later visits), which targets `$9F88` directly: banner, number, and the object is gone. RUN: type 4 left no object. RUN: slot 5 set to type `$35`, `$51` = the screen type, `$E4` = a real map record, bank 5 live, `$9F22` called with X = 5 on the labyrinth savestate.

regions.name: Init, type 1 (the progress recorder)
regions.description: `$7C/$7D` := `$52/$53` (the position the CONTINUE start-up will use), X++ and A := 4, then to `$9FC6`: the message object goes in slot X+1 with message 4. RUN: `$7C/$7D` = (8, 12), slot 6 = type `$34`, message 4. RUN: slot 5 set to type `$35`, `$51` = the screen type, `$E4` = a real map record, bank 5 live, `$9F22` called with X = 5 on the labyrinth savestate.

regions.name: Init, type 3 (a message), and the message object
regions.description: `$9FC4`: A := `$5E`, the record's sub-id (story 0-3, seal hints 12-20). `$9FC6`: `$0788,X` := A and `$0500,X` := `$34`: the slot becomes a type-`$34` message object (bank 6 `$99F8` moves `$0788` into `$0620`, which the dialogue routine `$8471` indexes through `$960F`). RUN: type 3 with sub-id 3 -> slot 5 type `$34`, message 3. RUN: slot 5 set to type `$35`, `$51` = the screen type, `$E4` = a real map record, bank 5 live, `$9F22` called with X = 5 on the labyrinth savestate.

regions.name: Init, type 7 (a shop after buying): the seal-4 test
regions.description: `JSR $A2E7` (the move-history test): equal (pass) goes on to `$9FD8`; else message 10 (`$0A`). RUN: with a history that fails the slot became message 10. RUN: slot 5 set to type `$35`, `$51` = the screen type, `$E4` = a real map record, bank 5 live, `$9F22` called with X = 5 on the labyrinth savestate.

regions.name: Seal 4 is released: message 11
regions.description: `$04B1` bit 3 set (corridor 4's seal), sound `$3F`, message 11. Reached from types 2, 6 and 7 when the pass test succeeds.

regions.name: Init, type 2 (the first shop): place the three items
regions.description: Three calls to `$A33F` put an item object in slots 6, 7 and 8 at the cells `$65`, `$67`, `$69` (x `$58`, `$78`, `$98`, y `$68`), and field 17 (`$069E`, `$069F`, `$06A0`) := `$5C`, `$D8`, `$DC`: a per-item value the item handler reads; its meaning is not established.

regions.name: Shop 1: the items' type
regions.description: Slots 6, 7 and 8 := type `$33` (the shop item). RUN: three `$33` in slots 6-8. RUN: slot 5 set to type `$35`, `$51` = the screen type, `$E4` = a real map record, bank 5 live, `$9F22` called with X = 5 on the labyrinth savestate.

regions.name: Shop 1: price and item ids
regions.description: Y := `$55` x 5 into the table `$A04E`: the first two bytes (a price in chips, little endian) go to every item's fields 25 and 26 (`$0758`, `$0770`); the next three bytes become the items' ids in field 16 (`$0680,6-8`). X ends at 9.

regions.name: Shop 1: the seal-4 test, else message 8
regions.description: `JSR $A2E7`: pass jumps to `$9FD8`; otherwise slot 9 becomes the message object with message 8. RUN: slot 9 = `$34`, message 8. RUN: slot 5 set to type `$35`, `$51` = the screen type, `$E4` = a real map record, bank 5 live, `$9F22` called with X = 5 on the labyrinth savestate.

regions.name: Shop 1 stock: 5 x [price lo][price hi][item][item][item]
regions.description: Indexed by `$55` x 5 (`$55` = 0-4 from `$A377` for sub-ids 58-67): 150, 1000, 400, 600, 2000 chips and the items `10 14 00 / 10 14 02 / 0D 0C 03 / 11 0C 04 / 06 0C 05` (item ids as the pick-up routine `$86BC` takes them; their names are not worked out here). One price per row, shared by the three items.

regions.name: Shop 2 stock: 5 x [price lo][price hi][item]
regions.description: Indexed by `$55` x 3: 50, 100, 150, 500, 300 chips for the items 2, 6, 1, 7, 8.

regions.name: Init, type 6 (the second shop): the item
regions.description: One item at cell `$67` (x `$78`, y `$68`) in slot 6 (type `$33`), field 17 := `$5C`.

regions.name: Shop 2: price and item
regions.description: Y := `$55` x 3 into the table `$A067`: price low and high to `$075E` / `$0776` (slot 6 fields 25, 26), the item id to `$0686` (field 16); X := 9.

regions.name: Shop 2: the seal-4 test, else message 7
regions.description: `JSR $A2E7`; pass: `$9FD8`; otherwise message 7 in slot 9. RUN: slot 9 = `$34`, message 7. RUN: slot 5 set to type `$35`, `$51` = the screen type, `$E4` = a real map record, bank 5 live, `$9F22` called with X = 5 on the labyrinth savestate.

regions.name: Screen object, every later frame: by type
regions.description: Type 8 -> the gate drivers `$A0F7`; type 6 -> `$A0DF`; type 1 -> the recorder `$A2B9`; every other type carries on at `$A0BF`.

regions.name: Screen object: the first shop's items
regions.description: `$0506 AND $0507 AND $0508` non-zero (all three item slots still occupied) returns. Otherwise (an item has been taken) with Start not held `$07A6-$07A8` := 1; either way on to `$A0E4`. RUN: with all three items present nothing happened.

regions.name: Screen object: the second shop's item
regions.description: `$0506` still occupied returns; empty goes on.

regions.name: Shop finished: record it, say thanks
regions.description: `$EFE9` sets the item flag `$5E` (this shop's sub-id, so the next visit is screen type 7), `$C048` removes the screen object, slot 9 := type `$34` with message 9. RUN: emptying slot 7 (shop 1) or slot 6 (shop 2) gave slot 5 removed, message 9 in slot 9, and bit 4 of byte 7 of the flag array set for sub-id 60. RUN: slot 5 set to type `$35`, `$51` = the screen type, `$E4` = a real map record, bank 5 live, `$9F22` called with X = 5 on the labyrinth savestate.

regions.name: The progress recorder, every frame
regions.description: Returns unless `$3C` = 0 (no weapon selected) and A is newly pressed (`$F5|$F6` bit 7). Then slots 5 and 6 are removed, `$0500` := 0 and a far call (inline `03 08 80`) goes to bank 3 `$8009` (-> `$832D`, beside the password encoder `$83AE`; presumably the password display - a lead, not entered). RUN: with `$3C` = 3 and A pressed nothing happened; with `$3C` = 0 the far call did not return in 400 frames.

regions.name: The progress recorder: leave
regions.description: After the far call returns: `$A0` := 3 (transition, warp-style exit), `$30` := `$20`, `$2F` := 3 (start mode 3, see the start-mode notes).

regions.name: Move-history test (seal 7, the round creature)
regions.description: Y = 6 down to 1: `$04F0,Y + $04EF,Y` must equal 8 (N 0 + S 8, W 2 + E 6 add to 8; 4 + 4 too). All six pairs equal: Z set (pass). Only history entries 0-6 are tested, not 7-9. RUN: `0 8 0 8 ...`, `2 6 2 6 ...` and ten 4s pass; a 2 followed by an 8 at entries 6-7 fails; entries 7-9 do not matter.
